newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - rally fades, prices up 1/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - rally fades, prices up 1/4.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended Tuesday's session 1/4 point higher after a bigger advance linked to the morning's fourth quarter Employment Cost Index fizzled.
"The market couldn't hold onto its gains," a municipal trader said. "I would have to categorize it maybe up 1/4 point on the day, not a lot of activity, but better than yesterday."
A municipal analyst agreed that muni cash ended 1/4 point higher overall. Bonds had been up 1/2 to 5/8 before their afternoon fade, he said.

Dollar bonds' progress mirrored the broader market, while high-grade issues ended the session three basis points firmer than Monday's close. Yields on high-grade issues had improved by about five basis points before the market's fade, he said.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 6/32 at 94-20/32 to yield 6.93 percent. The bond had been up well over a point after the U.S. Labor Department said the Employment Cost Index rose 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter. The wages and salaries component was also up 0.8 percent, while benefit costs gained 0.7 percent.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.9 percent rise for ECI. The report help subdue fears that the Federal Reserve will tighten credit at its Feb.4 open market committee meeting.
The bond market rally lost steam later following strong retail sales and consumer confidence data, analysts said.
On Wednesday, the market receives December durable goods figures. Economists polled by Reuters expect a 1.2 percent rise overall, and a 2.2 percent rise excluding defense orders.

If durables are bond friendly, two days of favorable numbers may help stir some action in municipals, a trader said. The danger, however, is that if the market firms, customers could see a selling opportunity, he said.
"If they pile on with the bid lists, the market will fail, that's for sure," he said.
What municipals needs now is some fresh paper, the trader said.
"We have no calendar, and that's not helping us," he said. "That gives direction."
A municipal analyst described pricing on Tuesday's new issues as firm to strong.

In negotiated action, Smith Barney Inc priced $133 million West Virginia School Building Authority capital improvement refunding revenue bonds series 1997. The bonds were priced at a top yield of 5.80 percent in 2022.
Lehman Brothers repriced $90 million Farmington, N.M., pollution control revenue refunding bonds, trimming the top yield to 6.375 percent from 6.45 percent in 2022.
Also Tuesday, Alex. Brown & Sons repriced $61.75 million New Jersey Health Care Financing Authority revenue bonds, trimming the top yield in 2027 to approximately 6.183 percent from of 6.20 percent.
In competitive action, Prudential Securities won $50 million West Virginia Housing bonds at a true interest cost of 5.848 percent.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed up 9/32 at 113-31/32. The March T-bond contract closed up 9/32 at 110-2/32. The MOB spread was 125 ticks.
